title: 4 Stocks I'm BUYING Before 2027
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
summary: Mark Roussin names four stocks he is buying before 2027, as technology shares sell off while earnings keep growing. He says he is not trying to predict the exact bottom and favours staged buying and some cash-secured puts rather than putting all his eggs in one basket. First is Nvidia, down below $210 from $240 a few weeks ago, on a forward P/E of 13 with an analyst average target near $340; data-centre revenue was about $89 billion, up about 120% year over year, with orders running through 2027 and into 2028. Second is AMD, on a forward P/E of 32.8 with an analyst average near $615 — he believes it is a $1,000 stock in the near future — as data-centre growth passes 100% and becomes over half the business. Third is Lam Research, garbled as 'Lamb Research' in the captions, which fell over 10% after record September-quarter revenue of about $8.2 billion, up about 54%; on a forward P/E just shy of 24 and an analyst average of $375, he would definitely buy at about 22 times or lower. Fourth is Sterling Infrastructure, on a P/E of 13 against 29% growth, a PEG below 1 and a backlog of about $4.3 billion, up over 115%, 92% of it mission-critical. The calls are NVDA — BUY, AMD — BUY, LRCX — CONDITIONAL_BUY (first tracked) and STRL — BUY (first tracked).

calls.price_at_call: was $240 a few weeks ago, dropped below $210 last week (stated); forward P/E 13x on next-fiscal-year EPS $9.28 (stated); analyst average target about $340, over 50% upside (stated)
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 2026-10-18; no flip) — stock one of four he is buying before 2027: 'one of the easiest buys in the market right now', a name he is most interested in accumulating as retail investors get shaken out while earnings keep growing.
calls.base_case: Nearly $100bn quarterly revenue, data centre about $89bn, up about 120% YoY; orders run through calendar 2027 and into 2028; Edge score 86; stock up roughly 10% over 12 months with higher highs/lows since April.
calls.bull_case: Full computing ecosystem (accelerators, networking, software, integrated systems), not just GPUs; AI demand could be large enough to support several winners and Nvidia remains extremely well positioned; earnings nearly doubling this year and +70% the next on his figures.
calls.bear_case: Competition is rising — AMD accelerators, hyperscaler custom chips, and Broadcom/Marvell benefiting from that trend — which he acknowledges, though he does not see it as winner-take-all.

calls.price_at_call: forward P/E 32.8x (stated); analyst average target about $615, over 15% upside (stated), high target $1,250; he believes it is a $1,000 stock in the very near future
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 2026-10-18, previously CONDITIONAL_BUY on 8/13 Oct; no flip) — stock two of four he is buying before 2027, interested in adding; he is less comfortable than with Nvidia but sees a huge pop potential.
calls.base_case: Data-centre growth over 100% YoY and now over half of total business; server CPU dominance plus Ryzen PCs give several growth legs; Edge score 73; shares up about 100% over 12 months.
calls.bull_case: Opportunity to keep taking server CPU share while building a much larger AI accelerator business; earnings expected +80% this year and over +100% next year, which he calls cheap at 32.8x forward.
calls.bear_case: His own caution: a great business does not automatically make a great stock to buy, and he is not as comfortable here as with Nvidia — the case depends on continued execution against tough comparisons.

calls.price_at_call: forward P/E just shy of 24x on 2027 earnings growth of 65% expected (stated); analyst average target $375, over 50% upside (stated); definite-buy trigger about 22x forward or lower (stated)
calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY, first tracked LRCX call for Mark Roussin (no flip) — stock three of four: Lam Research (captions garble it as 'Lamb Research'). He is increasingly interested after a >10% post-earnings sell-off and says 'if it continues to fall into around 22 times or even lower, I'm definitely buying before 2027.'
calls.base_case: September quarter revenue about $8.2bn, up about 54% YoY, adjusted EPS $2.20, operating margins about 40% — record revenue and profitability; biggest customers Micron, SK Hynix and TSMC are all rushing to add capacity; Edge score 78, shares still up 51% over 12 months.
calls.bull_case: More complex chips need more etching/deposition equipment, so AI chip demand directly creates equipment demand; capacity, not demand, is the bottleneck for its customers.
calls.bear_case: December guidance about $8.6bn disappointed versus expectations; supply-chain constraints may limit near-term shipments, and China was about 35% of September revenue with that share expected to decline significantly in December.

calls.price_at_call: P/E 13x on 29% earnings growth, PEG well below 1 (stated); lowest analyst forecast still near a doubling (stated); no share price stated
calls.thesis: BUY, first tracked STRL call for Mark Roussin (no flip) — stock four of four, the one he told viewers to wait for: highest upside potential on his list and a compelling way to own the physical side of the AI build-out; Edge score 88, higher than Nvidia's.
calls.base_case: Revenue growth over 100%, net income up about 120%, backlog about $4.3bn, up over 115% YoY; mission-critical projects are about 92% of E-infrastructure backlog — data centres, manufacturing and semiconductor facilities.
calls.bull_case: Sterling builds the facilities (land development, site prep, electrical, construction) whichever chip maker wins, so it does not need to pick the semiconductor winner; he sees the AI build-out in early-to-middle innings.
calls.bear_case: Political pressure on data centres (he expects it to blow over after the midterms); like the other three names it shares AI-capex exposure — if big tech cuts capex several could fall together — and far fewer analysts cover it, so targets are thinner evidence.
